title: Common
description: Shared definitions referenced by every Memory Engine contract schema. This file declares no root type; it exists only to host $defs.
$comment: CONTRACT v0. Design rules enforced throughout: (1) every object is additionalProperties:false so neither agent can smuggle in an undeclared field; (2) all timeline and source timings are RationalTime, never floats, because float seconds cannot round-trip OpenTimelineIO losslessly and cannot express 1001/30000 drop-frame rates exactly; (3) identity is content-addressed (BLAKE3) wherever the bytes determine the identity, and UUID only where a human or a clustering run created the entity; (4) no schema ever carries pixel data.

SchemaVersion.title: SchemaVersion
SchemaVersion.description: Contract version this record was written against. Frozen at 'v0' for the Phase 0 contract. A reader that does not recognise the value must refuse the record rather than guess -- see hard rule 7, no silent anything.

Blake3Hash.title: Blake3Hash
Blake3Hash.description: Lowercase hex BLAKE3-256 digest. The universal content address: same bytes anywhere in the world produce the same id, which is what makes every job idempotent.

Uuid.title: Uuid
Uuid.description: RFC 4122 UUID, lowercase. Used only for entities whose identity is NOT determined by content: person ids, cluster ids, user sessions, projects.

Slug.title: Slug
Slug.description: Short stable machine identifier, lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens and underscores. Used for ids that are authored by us rather than generated: track ids, act ids, check ids.

Timestamp.title: Timestamp
Timestamp.description: RFC 3339 instant with an explicit offset. Every wall-clock moment the system itself observes (ingest time, decision time, render time) is unambiguous by construction.

LocalDateTime.title: LocalDateTime
LocalDateTime.description: ISO 8601 date-time with NO offset, e.g. 2019-08-04T17:22:31. This is what a camera actually writes into EXIF DateTimeOriginal: a wall-clock reading with no timezone. Storing it as a naive local time and keeping the zone separate is the only lossless representation.

RationalTime.title: RationalTime
RationalTime.description: A time expressed as an exact rational: value frames (or samples) at the given rate. Maps 1:1 onto opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime. Seconds = value / rate. Never store seconds as a float in this contract.

value.description: Position or count in units of 1/rate. May be fractional to survive sample-accurate audio edits, but integral values are strongly preferred on video tracks.

TimeRange.title: TimeRange
TimeRange.description: Half-open interval [start_time, start_time + duration). Maps 1:1 onto opentimelineio.opentime.TimeRange. Half-open is deliberate and matches OTIO: it makes adjacent clips tile a timeline with no off-by-one frame.

Unit.title: Unit
Unit.description: A score normalised to [0,1]. Every model output in this contract is normalised before it is written, so fusion never has to know a model's native range.

Confidence.title: Confidence
Confidence.description: Calibrated probability in [0,1]. Distinct from Unit by intent: a Confidence is expected to be calibrated against a validation set and is therefore comparable to a threshold. A Unit is merely ordered.

NormalizedBox.title: NormalizedBox
NormalizedBox.description: Axis-aligned rectangle in normalised image coordinates: origin top-left, x to the right, y down, all values in [0,1] relative to the ORIENTED image (after EXIF rotation is applied). Normalised so a box computed on a 512px thumbnail is valid against the 6000px original without rescaling -- this is what lets analysis run on proxies and render run on sources.

rotation_deg.description: Clockwise rotation of the box about its own centre. Present only for crops that deliberately rotate, e.g. straightening a horizon in an album placement.

Point2D.title: Point2D
Point2D.description: Point in the same normalised, orientation-applied coordinate space as NormalizedBox. Landmarks may fall slightly outside [0,1] when a face is clipped by the frame edge, so the bounds here are deliberately loose.

AspectRatio.title: AspectRatio
AspectRatio.description: Exact aspect ratio as integers, e.g. 9:16 for a reel. Integers rather than a float so 'is this 16:9' is an equality test, not an epsilon comparison.

PerceptualHash.title: PerceptualHash
PerceptualHash.description: Perceptual hash used for near-duplicate bucketing. Bucketing is by Hamming distance on this hash; the bucket is then refined by embedding distance (build plan 4.2). Always carries its algorithm so a future algorithm change cannot silently invalidate existing buckets.
PerceptualHash.$comment: bits and hex must agree: bits == 4 * len(hex). A hash whose declared length disagrees with its payload silently poisons dedupe -- Hamming distance against a truncated or over-long digest is meaningless, and the resulting buckets would merge unrelated photos or split identical ones. The allOf below enforces the three permitted pairings rather than leaving the rule in prose.

bits.description: Hash length in bits. Enforced to equal 4 * len(hex).

hex.description: Lowercase hex digest. Its length is pinned to `bits` by the constraints below.

TimeSource.title: TimeSource
TimeSource.description: Where a capture time came from, ordered from most to least trustworthy. The ranking is load-bearing: event clustering weights a filename-derived date far less than an EXIF original, and an inferred date not at all for chronology-critical decisions.

TimeAssertion.title: TimeAssertion
TimeAssertion.description: A claim about when something was captured, together with how much we believe it. Modelling capture time as an assertion rather than a bare timestamp is what lets the system ingest a library where a third of the files have no EXIF date at all without either dropping them or lying about their chronology.

local.description: Wall-clock reading as recorded by the device, with no zone applied. Null when nothing in the file or its neighbours implies a time.

utc.description: Resolved instant, present only when the zone is actually known (explicit offset in metadata, or GPS-derived zone). Never fabricate this by assuming the machine's local zone -- that silently shifts an entire holiday by hours.

timezone.description: IANA zone name, e.g. Asia/Kolkata, when it could be determined from metadata or GPS coordinates.

utc_offset_minutes.description: Offset actually recorded in the file (EXIF OffsetTimeOriginal or QuickTime), when present.

precision.description: Granularity the assertion is actually good to. 'unknown' means we have no usable time at all, and consumers must exclude the item from chronology-ordered output rather than sorting it to the epoch.

inferred_from_media_ids.description: When precision came from neighbour_interpolation, the sibling records that bracketed this one. Recorded so the inference is auditable and can be recomputed when a neighbour's date is later corrected.

VectorSpace.title: VectorSpace
VectorSpace.description: Named embedding space. Two vectors may only be compared when their space matches exactly, including the model version that produced them -- a SigLIP 2 upgrade creates a NEW space, it does not reinterpret the old one.

VectorRef.title: VectorRef
VectorRef.description: Reference to an embedding held in the vector index. Embeddings are referenced rather than inlined so a MediaRecord stays small enough to page through 100k of them in a UI; the index owns the floats. Inline values are permitted ONLY for fixtures and tests, where self-containment matters more than size.

index_key.description: Row key in the sqlite-vec table. Required when storage is 'index'.

values.description: Raw float components. Permitted only when storage is 'inline'. Length must equal `dimensions`.

normalized.description: True when the vector is L2-normalised, which makes cosine distance a dot product. Every space in this contract stores normalised vectors.

allOf.$comment: storage=inline requires values; storage=index requires index_key. Encoded as if/then so a malformed VectorRef fails validation rather than silently losing the embedding.

ModelRef.title: ModelRef
ModelRef.description: Pin to an exact model in the registry. Carries the weights hash, not just a version string, because 'the same version' of a HuggingFace repo has changed weights under people before. A record produced by an unpinned model is not reproducible, and reproducibility is the product.

precision.description: Quantisation the weights were executed at. int8 and fp16 runs can differ from fp32 at the third decimal, which is enough to flip a borderline face match, so it is part of provenance.

ModelRun.title: ModelRun
ModelRun.description: One execution of one model against one record. Every score in this contract points at a run id, so 'why is this photo ranked 0.82' is always answerable and a model swap can be evaluated by replaying only the affected runs.

input_proxy_id.description: Which proxy the model actually saw. Analysis never touches originals (AGENTS.md hard rule 5), so this is normally set; null only for classical measures computed during ingest.

Score.title: Score
Score.description: A single scored value with a pointer back to the run that produced it.

raw_value.description: Model output before normalisation to [0,1], kept so a recalibration can be applied without re-running the model.

ConsentRef.title: ConsentRef
ConsentRef.description: Pointer into the consent ledger owned by services/api. Required on anything that leaves the device or touches a child's face. Hard rule: no network egress without a ledger entry, verified by the CI egress test.

Determinism.title: Determinism
Determinism.description: Everything needed to reproduce a plan byte-for-byte. Present on every artifact a planner emits (EDL, AlbumSpec). Hard rule 3: same plan + same sources = identical output, and that is only auditable if the plan says what produced it.

seed.description: Seed for every stochastic choice in planning (variant sampling, tie-breaking). Same seed + same inputs must yield the same plan.

inputs_digest.description: BLAKE3 over the canonical JSON of every input the planner read: candidate ids, parameters, model refs. Two plans with the same digest and the same planner version are guaranteed identical.
